author: Sclater, 1863
status: 여름철새 10만 마리 이상 · 나그네새 수만 마리 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 봄과 가을의 이동 무렵 우리나라 숲에 머물렀다 떠나는 여름철새이다. 숲속 참나무 등의 가지에 밥그릇 모양 둥지를 짓고, 5~6월에 녹청색 바탕에 적갈색 반점이 있는 알을 6~7개 낳는다. 흰배지빠귀와 비슷한 소리로 지저귄다. 한국, 중국, 러시아 등에 분포한다.

points.en: black spots on breast and flanks (female)

sexes.male: 머리, 등, 멱, 윗가슴이 회색이고 아랫가슴과 배는 흰색, 옆구리는 주황색이다. 날개와 꼬리는 어두운 회색이다.
sexes.female: 등이 갈색이고 배는 흰색이며, 옆구리는 주황색이고 가슴과 옆구리에 검은 반점이 있다.

art.subject: Grey-backed Thrush (Turdus hortulorum), adult male in breeding plumage (late spring in Korea): head, nape, back, rump, throat and upper breast plain blue-grey; wings and tail darker slate-grey; flanks and sides of the lower breast bright orange-rufous; centre of the lower breast and belly white; undertail coverts white; bill yellow to orange-yellow; dark brown eye; pale pinkish-brown legs.
art.pose: perched on an oak branch, side view
art.scene: Korean deciduous forest with oaks in late spring; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched on an oak branch: plain blue-grey head, back and upper breast, darker slate wings and tail, orange-rufous flanks, white belly, yellow bill
adult female, side view perched: olive-brown upperparts, whitish throat with dark streaks at the sides, greyish-buff breast spotted black, orange flanks with dark spots, white belly
art.build: Medium-sized thrush, about 23cm: a little shorter than a Brown-eared Bulbul, plumper and shorter-tailed. Rounded head; perches upright on branches and stands more horizontally on the ground. Bill straight, slightly shorter than the head. Legs medium length, pale. At rest the wingtips reach about the base of the tail. Tail medium length, square-ended. Feeds on the forest floor by hopping and pausing; sings from the canopy.
avoid: Do not paint a white supercilium; that is Eyebrowed Thrush.
Do not paint orange right across the breast; the male's breast is grey and the orange is only on the flanks.
Do not paint a black head and breast; that is the male Japanese Thrush.
Do not paint spots on the male's breast; only the female is spotted.
